nodes.label: Budgetella — personal finance app
nodes.rationale: Landing page states the product intent explicitly: no bank login, no ads, privacy-first — 'Your bank password, card details, constant notifications. We just want to help you know where your money goes.' Entry is manual/AI (receipt, voice) instead of bank connectivity.

nodes.label: Budgi — AI spending assistant
nodes.rationale: Privacy policy states the AI-assistant rationale: Budgi analyzes the user's own data for insights; data is anonymized, sent to Gemini only after explicit consent, never used for training, retained ≤30 days.

nodes.label: Face ID Lock
nodes.rationale: Stated rationale on the landing page and trust bar: 'Privacy by default' — biometric lock protects financial data on-device without server-side credentials.

nodes.label: Backup & Restore (JSON export)
nodes.rationale: Positioned as a differentiator in the comparison table ('Full data ownership (JSON export)') and as data portability in privacy/terms — users own the data they enter and can export it from Settings.

nodes.label: AI Receipt Scanning (OCR)
nodes.rationale: Stated rationale: 'Manual entry is optional' — AI reads amount, category, and date from a photo to remove entry friction; receipt photo is sent to Gemini only with explicit consent.

nodes.label: Google Analytics 4 (G-93JNEYMKHT)
nodes.rationale: Privacy policy's cookie section explains the tracking choice: GA4 used for anonymous traffic analysis only — no cross-site tracking, no advertising cookies.

nodes.label: Data Processing Agreement (DPA)
nodes.rationale: Privacy policy states all third-party processors (Firebase, Gemini, crash reporting) are bound by KVKK-compliant DPAs.

nodes.label: Firebase (Google Cloud) backend
nodes.rationale: Chosen as hosting/storage and auth provider; policy states AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit, and DPA-bound processing.

nodes.label: Google Gemini API
nodes.rationale: Privacy policy explains the AI-provider choice (Google LLC): anonymized spending summaries or receipt photos transmitted over an encrypted channel; contract forbids model training, display to other customers, and retention beyond 30 days; explicit user consent required.

nodes.label: KVKK — Turkish data protection law (Law 6698)
nodes.rationale: The Turkish legal pages are structured around KVKK: data-controller framing, Article 11 rights (learn, correct, delete, object), 30-day response obligation — the explicit reason the TR privacy page exists.

nodes.label: Budgetella Monorepo
nodes.rationale: Single repository intentionally hosts multiple independent sub-projects (iOS, Android, web, backend) to share Firebase infrastructure and keep cross-platform entitlement logic consistent.

nodes.label: Privacy-First Personal Finance Tracker
nodes.rationale: Core product identity: local-first storage, optional sync, no tracking, open source.

nodes.label: Hakkımızda (About)
nodes.rationale: Manifesto: finans sayılarla değil kararlarla ilgili; sadelik bir kural, özellik değil; 'bankalarla rekabet etmiyoruz, anlamlandırma yapıyoruz' — veri Türkiye'de, konuşma dili Türkçe, banka bağlantısız.

nodes.label: Ana Sayfa (Landing)
nodes.rationale: Bilinçli tasarım tercihi (FAQ'da açıkça belirtilmiş): banka bağlantısı yok — kullanıcı harcamalarını manuel, sesli veya fiş tarama ile girer; gizlilik (KVKK) ve Türkçe konuşan AI asistan Budgi, banka ve klasik bütçe uygulamalarına karşı ana farklılaştırıcı konumlandırma.

nodes.label: Gizlilik Politikası
nodes.rationale: Hassas alanlar (işlem açıklamaları, sohbet geçmişi) uçtan uca şifreli — şirket dahil hiç kimse okuyamaz; BDDK kapsamındaki açık bankacılık verisi toplanmaz; kontrollü üçüncü taraf paylaşımı (AWS, AI sağlayıcı, Sentry) gizlilik vaadiyle dengeleniyor.

nodes.label: Budgetella Budgeting App
nodes.rationale: Hub node inferred from the consistent 'budgetella' prefix shared by every screenshot and graphic filename; gives the ambiguous/unrelated image assets a single concrete target for review.

nodes.label: Cash & Multi-Card Tracking
nodes.rationale: Rationale stated in source: bank statements capture only ~60-70% of real spending because cash and multiple cards fall outside any single bank app, so a unified manual-entry model is needed for a full spending picture.

nodes.label: Expense Tracking
nodes.rationale: Rationale stated in sources: people underestimate monthly spending by ~30-40%; simply measuring/logging spending changes behavior (observer effect), so tracking is positioned as awareness, not restriction.

nodes.label: Monthly Budgeting
nodes.rationale: Rationale stated in sources: knowing where money goes is the only way to make better decisions with limited resources; positioned as a 30-minute setup plus a 15-minute monthly review routine, not a one-time task.

nodes.label: Privacy: No Bank Credentials Required
nodes.rationale: Explicit product decision stated in the comparison article: Budgetella never asks for bank account or card credentials — user-entered transactions keep financial data with the user; characterized as a conscious design choice.

nodes.label: 50/30/20 Rule
nodes.rationale: Rationale stated in sources: if fixed costs exceed 50% (common where rent alone passes the threshold), flexibility should come from the 'wants' bucket — the goal is awareness, not perfection.
